> **What this case shows** — the [Poincare case](../poincare-hrv-fantasia/index.qmd) gave the raw
> SD1/SD2. Toichi (1997) read two *clinical* indices off the same plot's **4-SD bounding box**
> (long axis **L = 4·SD2**, short axis **T = 4·SD1**): the **Cardiac Sympathetic Index**
> (CSI = L/T) and the **Cardiac Vagal Index** (CVI = log₁₀(L·T)). The ecosystem had SD1/SD2 but not
> these indices, so this case introduces a **newly-authored op**, `ecgHRVautonomic`. On real RR it
> reproduces NeuroKit2's `hrv_nonlinear` indices **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| **~1e-13**), and the finding:
> the **Cardiac Vagal Index is higher in the young (4.94) than the old (4.55)**, robust across the
> cohort (**5/5** young above the old mean) — the parasympathetic decline of autonomic aging.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for the cardiac autonomic balance: `ecgHRVautonomic(rr)` → `csi` (sympathetic),
`cvi` (vagal), `csi_modified` (a sensitive sympathetic marker).
**Way of thinking** — the Poincare cloud's *shape* is autonomic: its short axis (SD1, T) is vagal,
its long axis (SD2, L) is overall variability. CSI = L/T is the sympatho-vagal *balance*; CVI =
log(L·T) is the vagal *magnitude*. One plot, two branches of the autonomic nervous system.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioECG::ecgHRVautonomic()`; the clinical-index complement of
`ecgHRVpoincare()` (SD1/SD2) and `ecgHRVasymmetry()` (HRA).
:::

## Proposition

On a real 5-minute RR window (Fantasia f1y01), the newly-authored `ecgHRVautonomic` reproduces
NeuroKit2's Toichi indices bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~1e-13); and the Cardiac Vagal Index is higher in young
(4.94) than old (4.55), 5/5 young above the old mean.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and its fidelity: the ecosystem had SD1/SD2 but not the clinical CSI/CVI —
can we author them to reproduce the reference exactly, and does the vagal index track autonomic
aging?** The goal is to introduce `ecgHRVautonomic`, certify it bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2, and
read the age effect.

## Challenge & approach

The Toichi indices are read off the Poincare 4-SD box (L = 4·SD2, T = 4·SD1): CSI = L/T, CVI =
log₁₀(L·T), CSI_Modified = L²/T. We implement those exact formulas — with SD1 = SDSD/√2 (universal)
and SD2 = the geometric paired-projection (the convention in which the indices are defined) — as
`ecgHRVautonomic`, and check each index against NeuroKit2's `hrv_nonlinear`.

```
RR (Fantasia f1y01, 5-min) → ecgHRVautonomic → CSI 1.50, CVI 4.90, CSI_mod 520
                    vs NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear → bit-exact (max |diff| ~1e-13)
                    CVI young 4.94 > old 4.55 (5/5) → vagal decline with age
```

## Data

**Fantasia Database (PhysioNet)**: subject **f1y01** (young healthy adult), the first **5-minute** RR
window (392 intervals) — the same git-tracked root the sibling
[Poincare](../poincare-hrv-fantasia/index.qmd) and [HRA](../hra-fantasia/index.qmd) cases use; the
aging comparison uses all **10** subjects. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the Poincare 4-SD bounding box for f1y01 — the long axis L = 4·SD2 (red) and short axis T = 4·SD1 (blue) give CSI = L/T = 1.50. Right: the Cardiac Vagal Index across the 5 young and 5 old subjects — CVI is higher in the young (mean 4.94) than the old (4.55), all 5 young above the old mean, the parasympathetic decline of autonomic aging.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is the construction (CSI = long/short axis of the Poincare box);
the right panel is the finding (the vagal index falls with age).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Cardiac Sympathetic Index (CSI = L/T)** | **1.50** |
| **Cardiac Vagal Index (CVI = log₁₀(L·T))** | **4.90** |
| Modified CSI (L²/T) | **520** |
| op vs NeuroKit2 `hrv_nonlinear` (max \|diff\|) | **~1e-13** (bit-exact) |
| **young mean CVI → old mean CVI** | **4.94 → 4.55** |
| young subjects with CVI > old mean (of 5) | **5** |

The newly-authored op equals NeuroKit2 exactly, and the vagal index declines with age. Values trace
to [`artifacts/csi_summary.csv`](artifacts/csi_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`ecgHRVautonomic` fills a clinical gap — the ecosystem had the raw SD1/SD2 but not the Toichi CSI/CVI
indices — and it is exact: bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2. On real RR the Cardiac Vagal Index declines
with age, completing the autonomic-aging picture the DFA (α1 rises) and Poincare (SD1 falls) cases
began on the same cohort. The transferable takeaway: **the Poincare box gives you both autonomic
branches — CSI (L/T) for sympatho-vagal balance, CVI (log L·T) for vagal magnitude — and the vagal
index is the one that tracks the parasympathetic decline of aging.**

## Open questions

- CSI_Modified is the marker Jeppesen (2014) used for **seizure detection** from single-lead ECG;
  computing it in a sliding window over an ictal recording — and pairing it with the DFA α1 and HRA
  on the same beats — would test the multi-index autonomic signature of seizures. *Documented, not
  escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| cardiac autonomic indices (CSI/CVI/CSI_Modified) | `ecgHRVautonomic()` | PhysioECG |
| raw Poincare SD1/SD2 | `ecgHRVpoincare()` | PhysioECG |
| heart-rate asymmetry | `ecgHRVasymmetry()` | PhysioECG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **the window** — CSI/CVI are usually read on the 5-minute short-term HRV window; they need a stable
  Poincare cloud.
- **which index** — CSI (L/T) is the sympatho-vagal *ratio*; CVI (log L·T) is the vagal *magnitude*;
  CSI_Modified (L²/T) is the more sensitive sympathetic marker used clinically (seizure detection).
- **the SD2 convention** — the indices are defined on the *geometric* Poincare box, so `ecgHRVautonomic`
  uses the paired-projection SD2 (matching NeuroKit2); this differs by a small O(1/n) amount from the
  analytical closed-form SD2 that `ecgHRVpoincare` reports.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioECG)

a <- ecgHRVautonomic(rr)   # rr: data.frame(channel, rr_ms, time_sec)
a$csi   # 1.50 -- cardiac sympathetic index (L/T)
a$cvi   # 4.90 -- cardiac vagal index (log10(L*T)), falls with age

# reproduces NeuroKit2's hrv_nonlinear CSI/CVI/CSI_Modified bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~1e-13).
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/csi_summary.csv`](artifacts/csi_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks each
index, the bit-exact NeuroKit2 match, the vagal-decline finding and its cohort robustness (5/5), and
the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op; geometric-SD2 convention; aging descriptive on n=5+5).

## Erratum (PhysioRecipes 0.7.2) {#erratum}

`PhysioIO::readWFDB()` mis-defaulted the signal baseline on WFDB headers that
state the gain without a `(baseline)` annex — the style of the Fantasia and
original MIT-BIH headers — taking the gain as the baseline instead of the
spec default (the ADC zero). Fixed in PhysioIO 0.2.7; the corrected reader
agrees with the reference implementation `wfdb-python` **bit-for-bit**
(max |difference| = 0). The RR series this case uses were re-extracted with the
corrected reader.

Values corrected in this release:

| quantity | published | corrected |
|---|---|---|
| `csi` | 1.49624 | **1.50014** |
| `cvi` | 4.84935 | **4.90306** |
| `csi_modified` | 486.604 | **519.671** |
| `max_diff_nk` | 0 | **1.13687e-13** |
| `young_mean_cvi` | 4.8975 | **4.9436** |

The NeuroKit2 agreement is no longer exactly zero but at the
floating-point floor (max |difference| 1.1e-13): the corrected `CSI_Modified`
(~520) is large enough that the last bit differs. That is reported rather than
rounded away.

The case's finding is unchanged; only the numbers now come from correctly
scaled signals. Its artifact table, figure and replay bundle were all
regenerated from the corrected root by a committed generator under `agent/`.
